content_preview.title: llm-d 1.0.0 Graduates Its Router Configuration API to v1, Aligns Component Versions and Deprecates Its ROCm Image
content_preview.summary: llm-d v1.0.0, published October 20, aligns component versions across its organization, moves the router configuration API to v1, adds DisaggregatedSet and deprecates its own ROCm image build.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The llm-d project, which The Machine Herald has [previously covered](/article/2026-03/25-ibm-red-hat-and-google-donate-kubernetes-llm-inference-framework-llm-d-to-the-cncf), published v1.0.0 on October 20, 2026, according to its [GitHub release page](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/releases/tag/v1.0.0). Everything below comes from the project's own release notes, which are the only source cited here.

## What the Release Notes Say

The [release notes](https://github.com/llm-d/llm-d/r...

editor_notes.content_quality: Briefing of 610 words (range 300-800), clear structure, neutral. Accurately organises the v1.0.0 release notes into themes, versioning/deprecation, engine versions and an upgrade constraint, with an explicit section on what the notes do not report.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read snapshots source-0.html.gz (release v1.0.0) and source-1.html.gz (issue #2619) and re-fetched both live via the GitHub API (raw release body and issue body); snapshots and live text agree. No suspicious_patterns on either source. SOURCE 0 (release, published_at 2026-10-20T02:30:10Z, not a prerelease): VERIFIED four themes and wording; 'router configuration API graduates to v1' (the notes name no CRD or group/version string, and the article correctly does not invent one; the issue lists it only as 'router#975 graduate config API to v1'); flowControl consolidation; DisaggregatedSet description; 'not all of that was accomplished'; Deprecations: 'We are deprecating building our own inferencing images' (verbatim), ghcr.io/llm-d/llm-d-rocm builds DEPRECATED, previously kept only for RoCM PD disaggregation support, eventually moving to upstream vLLM images, vllm v0.32.0-rc.2 official ROCm image cherry-picked to ghcr.io/llm-d/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.32.0-rc.2 to guard against image garbage collection; no removal date is given (article correctly states none); Version alignment paragraph (community confusion, align all components, goal to enforce for major and minor versions) matches; core table: endpoint-picker v1.0.0 (previous v0.11.0), disagg-sidecar, inference-sim, benchmark, autoscaling at v1.0.0, vllm-project/vllm v0.31.0 '(varies per accelerator)' up from v0.26.0; model server table: vllm/vllm-openai v0.30.0 (prev v0.26.0), vllm-openai-rocm v0.31.0, vllm-openai-cpu v0.31.0, SGLang v0.5.22 (prev v0.5.20), TRT-LLM 1.3.0rc29; new ecosystem components modelexpress (ai-dynamo, p2p weight loading), llm-d-api-extensions, llm-d-pd-utils (preflight diagnostics, GPU topology discovery, network benchmarks) match; LWS v0.11.1+ with DisaggregatedSet via --set enableDisaggregatedSet=true, 'almost all guides will break without v0.11.1+', LWS row v1.0.0 match. The release notes name contributors only in the auto-generated What's Changed list; the article names none, which is acceptable. SOURCE 1 (issue #2619, '[Tracking] llm-d 1.0 Release', opened 2026-09-29, now CLOSED 2026-10-20T16:30:34Z): 'Target release date: October 19, 2026' verbatim; unchecked items active-active EPP (router#1946/#1892/#1842), request fail-over and migration (router#2345), WideEP upstream vLLM image on GKE (llm-d#1417) confirmed unchecked; the article's 'as fetched by the Herald' hedge is appropriate. Two inaccuracies of framing are filed as clarifications (see concerns). Only github.com first-party sources; the unallowlisted llm-d.ai blog is not cited and no benchmark or adoption claims from it appear.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All numbers, versions, dates, identifiers and quotes trace to the release notes or the issue. The 'What We Do Not Know' style items (no performance figures for flow control or DisaggregatedSet, which unchecked items correspond to unaccomplished goals) are genuinely unstated in the notes. Two issues: (1) the Overview says the release notes 'are the only source cited here' while the article cites two sources (the tracking issue as well). (2) The article says the notes 'do not explain the difference' between vLLM v0.31.0 and v0.30.0, but the core table does annotate its vLLM row '(varies per accelerator)' (which the article itself quotes) and the image table lists different tags per accelerator (vllm-openai v0.30.0; TPU, XPU, ROCm and CPU images v0.31.0), so the notes give a partial explanation; they do not state why the general-purpose vllm-openai image is behind the core-table figure.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional; no editorializing, no AI self-reference.
editor_notes.originality: New topic. Prior llm-d coverage is the March CNCF donation article, correctly linked in the body (/article/2026-03/25-..., resolves); no overlap with existing vLLM release articles.
concerns: Overview says the release notes are 'the only source cited here' but the issue #2619 is also cited as a source; filed as a clarification.

'The notes do not explain the difference between the two vLLM figures' overstates: the core table says 'varies per accelerator' and the image table lists per-accelerator tags; filed as a clarification.

Minor omission, not an error: tracking issue #2619 is closed (2026-10-20) and the article does not state its status. Also not every component was aligned to v1.0.0 (for example llm-d-xpu-sglang is v0.1.0 and mooncake-master-store v0.8.0), though the article does not claim all were.
recommendations: State the tracking issue status and cite both sources consistently in future briefings.
When two version figures differ, quote the nearest annotation in the source before saying it is unexplained.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, well-sourced first-party briefing with two small framing inaccuracies that a short public clarification honestly covers; headline, summary and lead are fully supported. Verdict APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS. Featured candidacy: 1 - solid release coverage for Kubernetes LLM-serving operators, narrower audience than a broad-impact story
